decisive_items: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
Blood cell count showed hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)
Elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)
response.rationale: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion is a defining clonal marker of chronic eosinophilic leukemia; the hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase/B12, and skin involvement fit this diagnosis more specifically than broader hypereosinophilic syndrome or histiocytic disorders.

rejected.why: Elevated tryptase is nonspecific; biopsy shows histiocytic infiltration, not mast cell aggregates.
Less specific than CEL because the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion indicates a clonal eosinophilic neoplasm.
Overly broad and does not account for the specific fusion gene.
Skin lesions and eosinophilia are nonspecific and lack the defining genetic marker.
Histiocytic infiltrate is present, but the fusion gene and eosinophilia point to CEL.
CD1a negativity and only weak S-100 staining argue against Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
